St. Clair College Women's Basketball has landed a hometown talent. Maya Fuerth, a 5'9" guard out of St. Joseph's High School, is transferring in after two seasons with the Wilfrid Laurier Golden Hawks, where she started 14 games and averaged 6.5 points per game in 2025-26.
Before Laurier, Fuerth helped St. Joseph's to an OFSAA silver medal and earned WECSSAA All-City MVP honours, along with Basketball Ontario championships with the Tecumseh Saints on the club circuit.
Head coach Andy Kiss on what she brings to the Saints: an inside-outside skill set, sharp footwork, a willingness to finish through contact, real three-point range, and versatility on defense across multiple positions.
Fuerth will also study Fitness and Health Promotion at St. Clair while suiting up for the 2026-27 season.

text.vimeo:1234711698:
The Windsor Lancers went into Kingston and knocked off the unbeaten Queen’s Golden Gaels.

Windsor beat the defending Yates Cup champions 25-22 on Saturday, handing Queen’s its first loss of the season. The Lancers (5-2) have now won four straight, and the Gaels fall to 5-1.

Kareame Cotton showed again why he’s in the conversation for the Hec Crighton Trophy. The Lancers quarterback went 17-for-27 for 284 yards and two touchdowns. He also kept the Queen’s defence guessing with his legs, running for 94 yards on 10 carries to lead all rushers.

His two touchdown passes give him 25 on the season, adding to the school record he set last week.

Fifth-year receiver Colby Ginn was his favourite target. Ginn caught eight passes for 182 yards and both Windsor touchdowns, including a 27-yarder in the second quarter and a 20-yarder early in the fourth. His longest catch went for 82 yards.

Kicker Alex Patrinos went 3-for-3 on field goals, from 34, 23 and 38 yards, and finished with 11 points.

The Windsor defence did its part, too. The Lancers picked off Queen’s quarterback Ashton St.Germain three times, with interceptions from Titus Lyles, Kevin Rakowska and Derek Anderson. Melyk George and Kage Bildfell each had a sack, and Windsor held the Gaels to 48 yards on the ground.

It went down to the wire. Ginn’s second touchdown put Windsor up 25-14 early in the fourth quarter. St.Germain answered with a two-yard touchdown run, and Jayden Gurzi-MacDonald ran in the two-point convert to make it 25-22 with 10:34 left. The Lancers defence held from there.

Windsor outgained Queen’s 447-328 in total offence and controlled the ball for 33:32.
